originalBroadTransactionTimeout.explanation: The original scheduler completed readiness successfully; its later transaction took 106.761 seconds. These failure/early-exit probes do not establish the cause of that post-handshake delay or demonstrate a broad-suite fix.

execution.scope: Four controlled real-child probes of scheduleReplace, outside the tool sandbox; no actual updater transaction or executable replacement was performed.
execution.baselineCommitBinding: Baseline HEAD was checked separately before probing; both baseline reports captured the production-source SHA at runtime.
execution.afterCommitBinding: Both after reports captured exact HEAD, production-source SHA, clean tracked status before/after, and probe SHA at runtime.

scripts.capture: Reconstructed verbatim from the recorded initial apply_patch tool write. Script hash was not captured at execution time.
Snapshot of the retained script after the recorded mode-extension patch, as used for the early-exit run. Script hash was not captured at execution time.
Retained script; its hash was captured at runtime in both after reports.

redactions: Absolute temporary fixture paths were removed from each embedded observation. Original raw reports are identified by byte count and SHA256; all other report fields are preserved.
limitations: Baseline script hashes were computed when archiving, not at execution. The first script snapshot was reconstructed from the recorded tool write; it is not contemporaneous script-hash attestation.

The probes inject real controlled children that fail to start or exit with code 7. They verify event delivery, prompt fail-closed rejection, and unchanged fixture bytes; they do not run a full Windows update.
All four runs retain the original owned nonce lock on handshake failure. No claim is made that keeping this lock alone revokes an already running sidecar.
An observed child error/exit takes precedence over readiness. No atomic guarantee is claimed for an OS exit whose JavaScript event has not yet been delivered.
Local probes do not substitute for authoritative CI or release matrices.
